A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Finite Group|finite group]] and $p$ a [[Definition:Prime Number|prime]] dividing $\order G$.
Then $G$ has an element of [[Definition:Order of Group Element|order]] $p$.

B_source.statement:
Let the [[Definition:Cyclic Group|cyclic group]] $\Z / p \Z$ act on a finite set $X$.
Then every orbit has size $1$ or $p$, so:
:$\card X \equiv \card {\map {\operatorname {Fix} } X} \pmod p$

substitutions.the set X: p-tuples in G with product e

derived.fixed tuples: constant tuples (g, ..., g) with g^p = e

object_map.reformulation: Encode elements with g^p = e as the fixed points of a rotation action, and count them modulo p.

validity_conditions: Rotation must preserve the product condition, which holds as cyclic shifts of a product equal to e are conjugate to it.
p must be prime, so that orbit sizes divide p and g^p = e with g non-identity forces order exactly p.
proof_plan:
Let $X = \set {\tuple {g_1, \ldots, g_p} \in G^p: g_1 g_2 \cdots g_p = e}$.
The last entry is determined by the others, so $\card X = \order G^{p - 1} \equiv 0 \pmod p$.

If $g_1 g_2 \cdots g_p = e$ then $g_2 \cdots g_p g_1 = g_1^{-1} e g_1 = e$.
Hence cyclic rotation defines an action of $\Z / p \Z$ on $X$.

The fixed points are the constant tuples $\tuple {g, \ldots, g}$ with $g^p = e$.
By the source result, their number is $\equiv \card X \equiv 0 \pmod p$.
